ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Wilma Mankiller — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Review five weeks after thymectomy: recovery, pathology, azathioprine monitoring, the prednisone taper, and kidney care

text.paragraph: Ms. Mankiller returns five weeks after a robotic thymectomy, with two nights in hospital and no postoperative weakness or breathing problem. The pathology showed thymic follicular hyperplasia and no thymoma. The port sites have healed, and she took acetaminophen, not anti-inflammatory medicines, for the pain. Her eyelids have not drooped for three weeks. She raised azathioprine to 100 mg daily after two weeks, as planned, by telephone. The blood tests planned for two, four and six weeks after starting azathioprine were not done: the orders were placed at this clinic, she was preparing for surgery, and no one followed them up. She has had no fever, sore throat, bruising or jaundice. She is back at work three days a week. Home blood pressure readings are about 118/76. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1980-07-13; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 124/80 mm Hg; weight 64.8 kg
Three healed port sites on the right; lungs clear
No ptosis after one minute of upgaze
Neck and limb strength 5 of 5 without fatigue

Drooping eyelids and double vision for six weeks, worse in the evening, with fatigable weakness of the arms and neck, tiring when chewing and a nasal voice after long talks; a disorder of the neuromuscular junction suspected
S — Synthetic presenting problem, resolved at the second visit when antibodies and nerve testing established myasthenia gravis.
Generalized myasthenia gravis, acetylcholine receptor antibody positive, MGFA class IIa, without thymoma; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented myasthenia gravis of 1934

S — Synthetic antibody level, electrodiagnosis, class and treatment; the diagnosis less than a year after the crash, and recovery with Cherokee medicine people, surgery and drug therapy, are documented (D).
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (hereditary, as she has described it), with normal kidney function; to be staged
S — The hereditary polycystic kidney disease is documented (D) from her later public account; its detection before the index date, and every value, are synthetic.
Recovery from major trauma in a head-on car crash last year: fractures of both legs, ribs and face, with many operations; walks independently, with a cane on rough ground
S — The crash, the operations and the injuries are documented (D); the current function is synthetic.
Long-term glucocorticoid therapy for myasthenia gravis, with monitoring of glucose, blood pressure, weight, bone health, mood, sleep, eyes and infection
Azathioprine as steroid-sparing therapy, with blood count and liver test monitoring
Acquired absence of the thymus after robotic extended thymectomy for myasthenia gravis (pathology: thymic follicular hyperplasia, no thymoma)
